British domestic holidays are being pushed to their highest levels since Covid

The start of the peak summer season is set to bring millions of drivers on to British roads, with concerns of traffic chaos as the port of Dover faces its biggest test yet of new EU border controls.

The semi-functioning entry-exit system (EES) is credited, along with the heatwaves and fears about flights after the war in Iran, with helping push British domestic holidays to its highest levels since Covid halted international travel.

Motoring organisations expect this Friday to kick-off the busiest summer weekend for domestic leisure trips.

The port of Dover is bracing for long tailbacks as thousands of holidaymakers join lorries at Britain’s main Channel ferry crossing from 6am.

French border police, situated at Dover, will manually register non-EU travellers for EES. The new £40m automated facility built to speed through passengers is unable to operate due to software problems in the technology in France.

Even though the French police aux frontières (PAF) will not be able to carry out the biometric registration required by EES – photographing and fingerprinting – the additional time needed to create a file for each visitor could still lead to long queues at the border, the port fears.

About 7,500 cars travelling to France are expected at Dover on Friday, and 10,000 on Saturday, as peak summer season begins.

The port has urged holidaymakers to use only main roads when driving to the port, and arrive no more than two hours before their booked sailing.

Eurotunnel, operator of LeShuttle, which takes vehicles through the Channel tunnel, said that it did not anticipate delays as summer traffic built up. As at Dover, border police will still not be registering biometric information from its car passengers for EES this summer. Eurotunnel has likewise spent millions of pounds on automated processing kiosks which cannot yet be brought into service.

Elsewhere, the RAC and Inrix expect the worst of the traffic on Friday in areas of the M25 around Greater London linking to the M3 to the southwest, as more than 14 million drivers make a getaway this weekend.

With most schools in England and Wales closing this weekend for the summer, most leisure journeys will take place on Saturday, the RAC said, as part of the biggest domestic getaway since 2022.

The Port of Dover has declared it has done "absolutely everything" to prepare for the upcoming summer getaway, despite significant concerns over potential delays stemming from new EU border checks.

Doug Bannister, chief executive of the Kent port, expressed his frustration, calling it "very disappointing" that a new £40 million processing facility, built specifically for the EU’s Entry Exit System (EES), remains unused for car passengers because the necessary EU technology has not been activated.

The EES, fully implemented in April, requires non-EU nationals, including British travellers, to have their fingerprints and photographs taken upon entering the Schengen Area.

While this process typically occurs at foreign airports for most UK citizens, it is also conducted at the Port of Dover, Eurotunnel’s Folkestone terminal, and London St Pancras railway station, all of which operate juxtaposed border controls.

The port experienced a "critical incident" during the May half-term, with waiting times reaching four-and-a-half hours for approximately 8,500 outbound tourist vehicles.

Mr Bannister recently warned MPs that the port faces "repeated episodes of severe congestion" this summer unless the EU grants greater flexibility for the EES, a concession that has yet to materialise.

Most schools in England and Wales break up for the summer holidays at the end of this week or early next week, while the academic year has already ended in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

The Port of Dover expects to have about 7,500 outbound cars on Friday, rising to nearly 10,000 on Saturday.

The end of next week will be even busier, with about 10,500 outbound cars on both July 24 and 25.

It was previously hoped that many of these would complete their EES registrations at the new Western Docks facility, which is equipped with 84 kiosks to record biometric details.

But the French authorities have not switched the kiosks on, and no date has been set for when that will happen.

Mr Bannister said: “We delivered our Western Docks facility after investing £40 million of our capital.

payload.title: Dover varautuu kesälomaliikenteen ruuhkiin EU:n uusien rajatarkastusten keskellä
payload.summary: Britannian kesälomakauden vilkkain viikonloppu tuo teille yli 14 miljoonaa autoilijaa samalla, kun Doverin satama valmistautuu EU:n uuden rajajärjestelmän tähänastiseen suurimpaan kesätestiin.
payload.content:
Britannian kesälomakauden vilkkain viikonloppu tuo maan teille yli 14 miljoonaa autoilijaa, ja Doverin satamassa varaudutaan pitkiin jonoihin. Britannian tärkein Englannin kanaalin lauttayhteys joutuu samalla kovaan testiin EU:n uuden rajanylitystietojärjestelmän käyttöönoton jälkeen.

Doverissa valmistaudutaan jonoihin

Tuhansien lomailijoiden odotetaan saapuvan Doveriin perjantaina aamukuudesta lähtien, jolloin henkilöautot liittyvät satamaan jonottaviin rekkoihin. Autoilujärjestöt ennakoivat perjantain käynnistävän kesän vilkkaimman kotimaan lomaliikenteen viikonlopun.

Dover on Britannian tärkein autolauttojen kanaalinylityspaikka, ja lomailijat joutuvat jakamaan satamaan johtavan liikenteen rekkojen kanssa. Ruuhkahuoli kohdistuu erityisesti perjantaiaamuun, jolloin matkustajien määrän odotetaan kasvavan kesän huippuviikonlopun alkaessa.

Sataman toimitusjohtajan Doug Bannisterin mukaan Dover on tehnyt kaiken mahdollisen liikenteeseen valmistautumiseksi. EU:n EES-järjestelmää varten rakennettu 40 miljoonan punnan käsittelylaitos on silti yhä käyttämättä autolla matkustavien osalta, koska tarvittavaa EU-teknologiaa ei ole aktivoitu.

Tilanne on satamalle tähän asti suurin uuden järjestelmän kesäkoe. Vaikka kaikkia matkustajille tarkoitettuja toimintoja ei käytetä, uudet rajajärjestelyt ovat lisänneet huolta käsittelyn sujuvuudesta.

Biometristen tietojen kerääminen viivästyy

Huhtikuussa kokonaisuudessaan käyttöön otettu EES edellyttää, että Schengen-alueelle saapuvilta EU:n ulkopuolisten maiden kansalaisilta, myös brittiläisiltä matkustajilta, otetaan sormenjäljet ja valokuva. Tänä kesänä Doverissa ei kuitenkaan rekisteröidä autoilla saapuvien biometrisiä tietoja.

Sama koskee Kanaalitunnelin LeShuttle-junaa operoivaa Eurotunnelia. Yhtiö on käyttänyt miljoonia puntia automaattisiin käsittelykioskeihin, joita ei vielä voida ottaa käyttöön. Eurotunnel ei tästä huolimatta odota kesäliikenteen aiheuttavan viivästyksiä.

Ruuhkia odotetaan myös Lontoon ympärille

RAC:n ja liikennetietoyhtiö Inrixin mukaan perjantain pahimpia ruuhkia odotetaan Lontoon ympärillä M25-kehätiellä, erityisesti sen M3-moottoritielle johtavilla osuuksilla lounaaseen päin. Suurin osa vapaa-ajan matkoista tehdään kuitenkin lauantaina, kun useimmat Englannin ja Walesin koulut jäävät kesälomalle.

RAC arvioi viikonlopusta Britannian suurinta kotimaan lomaliikenteen lähtöä sitten vuoden 2022. Kotimaanlomien määrä on nousemassa korkeimmalle tasolle sitten korona-ajan. Kehitystä ovat vauhdittaneet helleaallot, huoli lentomatkustamisesta Iranin sodan jälkeen sekä EES-järjestelmän keskeneräinen toiminta.
summary_bullets: Britannian teille odotetaan viikonlopuksi yli 14 miljoonaa autoilijaa.
Doverin 40 miljoonan punnan EES-käsittelylaitos ei ole vielä käytössä automatkustajille.
Pahimpia ruuhkia ennakoidaan Doverin lisäksi Lontoon M25-kehätielle.
payload.journalist_note: EES:n yleinen käyttöönotto ja automatkustajien biometrisen rekisteröinnin viivästyminen on erotettu tekstissä toisistaan.

article.source_text:
British domestic holidays are being pushed to their highest levels since Covid The start of the peak summer season is set to bring millions of drivers on to British roads, with concerns of traffic chaos as the port of Dover faces its biggest test yet of new EU border controls. The semi-functioning entry-exit system (EES) is credited, along with the heatwaves and fears about flights after the war in Iran, with helping push British domestic holidays to its highest levels since Covid halted international travel. Motoring organisations expect this Friday to kick-off the busiest summer weekend for domestic leisure trips. The port of Dover is bracing for long tailbacks as thousands of holidaymakers join lorries at Britain’s main Channel ferry crossing from 6am.

Eurotunnel, operator of LeShuttle, which takes vehicles through the Channel tunnel, said that it did not anticipate delays as summer traffic built up. As at Dover, border police will still not be registering biometric information from its car passengers for EES this summer. Eurotunnel has likewise spent millions of pounds on automated processing kiosks which cannot yet be brought into service. Elsewhere, the RAC and Inrix expect the worst of the traffic on Friday in areas of the M25 around Greater London linking to the M3 to the southwest, as more than 14 million drivers make a getaway this weekend. With most schools in England and Wales closing this weekend for the summer, most leisure journeys will take place on Saturday, the RAC said, as part of the biggest domestic getaway since 2022.

The Port of Dover has declared it has done "absolutely everything" to prepare for the upcoming summer getaway, despite significant concerns over potential delays stemming from new EU border checks. Doug Bannister, chief executive of the Kent port, expressed his frustration, calling it "very disappointing" that a new £40 million processing facility, built specifically for the EU’s Entry Exit System (EES), remains unused for car passengers because the necessary EU technology has not been activated. The EES, fully implemented in April, requires non-EU nationals, including British travellers, to have their fingerprints and photographs taken upon entering the Schengen Area.
